### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 50 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7e8cf4f1934db928891edf7407d23ce1b1df3ce1` — the merge of head `4412d2ffd37cc7c5f763f809115ae7695abfb895` into base `8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7e8cf4f1934db928891edf7407d23ce1b1df3ce1 && git checkout 7e8cf4f1934db928891edf7407d23ce1b1df3ce1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e 4412d2ffd37cc7c5f763f809115ae7695abfb895 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e && git merge --no-ff 4412d2ffd37cc7c5f763f809115ae7695abfb895

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8e63ed877771d6f3492309e596fb5422b3f0898e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4cbd2fca9faeaa5e7ab0116e5ff068ad3ed46b13`
Local-runs: none

I read the diff against the base branch `claude/area-A2-31908-p4a` at `3bcc3320` (#33476): 9 files. I checked it against seat ruling 6884540128 items 2 and 3.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Item 2 (S4): fault classes match the ruling.** Only `CanonicalFormError` and `SignedBodyError` are chain-local:
  - a row a canonical rule refuses (`readWindow`);
  - a malformed checkpoint of the chain (`headOf` → `ChainFault`; `listedIn` → `ChainFault` for its own chain, `skip` for another; `sealLate`'s holders).

  `writeChains` swallows only a `ChainFault` whose `chainKey` is the chain being written. Every other throw (lock lapse, signer, crypto, storage, Q6) still propagates and aborts the object's pass. A skipped chain stays out for the rest of the pass: `readWindow` and `writeChains` both test `skipped`.
- **Per-chain cursor.** `cursors` is built from each chain's `window` checkpoints at or past the floor. `cursorOf` takes the max of the floor and the chain's cursor. A chain with nothing past the floor (a previously skipped one included) restarts at the floor, so it resumes as `window` from its own oldest unsealed window. `sealLate` treats a row as late only before its chain's cursor, which replaces the old `resumed` set.
- **`sealed_through`.** The watermark passed in is `max(watermark, min(start, stuckFrom()))`. It is evaluated after `readWindow`, so a skip met while reading that window already holds it back. A skip met while writing that window has `from ≥ start`, so `sealed_through = start` does not pass it either. It starts from the floor, so it never drops below it. This matches the ruling: it never advances past a window a skipped chain leaves unsealed.
- **The report.** The `error` names the object, chain, fault and window. It repeats once per cause per `REPORT_REPEAT_MS` and is forgotten once the chain is sealed again.
- **Item 3, which matches the ruling.** `adoptHostCryptoProvider` is taken only when `options.cryptoProvider === undefined`, so an explicit provider is never overridden. `armSealer: false` from the host only disarms; it never turns on an app's `armSealer: false`. `handHostCryptoToAppAuditPlugin` acts only on an `instanceof` the class `serve` itself imports, so it never feeds a lookalike. An app bundling its own copy of the class fails `instanceof` and is left alone, which is fail-safe. Nothing throws or refuses the boot. D3's once-at-`error` report still covers an instance left without a provider. The provider is read lazily at `startSealer`, after the hand-over at `kernel.use`.
- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on both packages. This is correct: `AuditPlugin` gains a public method, and the sealer seals strictly more than before (a chain-local fault used to stop every chain).
- **should-fix S1: re-read cost while a chain stays skipped.** The floor stays at the skipped chain's window (by design). Every pass then walks every window from there to `due`, and a window whose rows all belong to chains already sealed past it does not count toward `MAX_WINDOWS_PER_PASS`. So while one chain stays faulty, each hourly pass re-reads every row of the object since that window, and the work grows by one window an hour without bound. Bound it, for example with a separate, larger cap on uncounted windows, or by seeking from the minimum per-chain cursor of the chains that still have rows. It is not a correctness fault, and the fix is the operator's, so it does not block this PASS. Track it in P4b2 or in a card.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch`, `@objectstack/cli: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. This is correct for a non-protocol widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The base is a branch (#33476), not `main`. Retarget to `main` after #33476 merges, and the ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head on `main`.
- The verify-side question you sent the seat (a window where the skipped chain is the only chain → no verdict, `ok` stays true) does not touch this diff. Ruling item 2 says verify stays loud, so that answer may need its own pin in P4c.

## Review carry — PASS stands

Head-sha: `22d4da3f6ea47cf704793e3012f02a5050f5f7ba`

I read the delta `4cbd2fca...22d4da3f`. It is test-only: two pins in `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`, and `sealer.ts` is unchanged. The pins cover seat ruling 6885452378's preconditions:
- **Window-major.** A dense chain and a sparse chain reach the same newest `window` checkpoint after each pass, with no `late`. The ablation (a per-chain budget) turns it red.
- **No late sweep.** A skipped chain recovers into `window` checkpoints (seq 0 and 1), and the only `late` checkpoint is the healthy chain's own. The ablation (the every-chain late rule) turns it red.

My PASS at `4cbd2fca9faeaa5e7ab0116e5ff068ad3ed46b13` carries to this head (Regen-provenance: test-pin-only move). S1 is tracked to P4b2. Before landing, retarget the base to `main`; the ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
